steps.note: loop head: burst 403s (zhihu rate wall, self-heals in ~15 min) used to die as a bare 15s wait timeout that named nothing

time-based settle, NOT a DOM wait: a burst-403 response never parses into a DOM in this engine (document.documentElement is undefined), so a readyState predicate burns its full timeout on exactly the wall this flow exists to classify. The DOM wait lives on the landed path (read), where a DOM exists
issue #73: a 403 document reads verdict unknown with facts.doc_status=403; content question page reads landed. Network facts, no DOM dependency — this classifies a wall a DOM wait cannot even see
issue #72: content page → jump straight to the read path

budget on the reserved steps_done counter, NOT a window counter: a wall-page navigation resets the JS context, so window.* retry counters silently restart at 1 every round and the loop never converges (dogfood 2026-09-22). steps_done is executor-maintained — 30 executions ≈ 5 wall retries
short spacing between in-flow retries (eval await budget caps this at seconds; long waits are the caller's job)
back-jump to the loop head (truthy on the executor counter is always true — the jump itself)

args.script: throw new Error('zhihu wall persists after ' + {{steps_done}} + ' step executions — verdict=' + JSON.stringify({{v}}) + '. Burst 403 self-heals in ~15 min: park, then rerun this flow with the same session_id (cookies stay warm).')

steps.note: the 15-minute backoff belongs to the CALLER (cron rerun), not to a flow holding a session — the receipt says exactly that
the only DOM wait in the flow, reachable only on verdict landed — a DOM is guaranteed to exist there
